text: ← Foundations contents THE LEARNING PATH WHAT YOU WILL LEARNEstimate the helium mass fraction from the neutron-to-proton ratio. 01The hot early universe In the early universe, reactions converted protons and neutrons into one another. Expansion and cooling made those reactions fall behind, and some neutrons decayed. Near the onset of efficient nucleosynthesis, a useful estimate is neutron : proton ≈ 1 : 7. Predicting that ratio requires weak-interaction and expansion calculations. 02Two neutrons and two protons make helium-4 Take 2 neutrons and 14 protons. If almost all neutrons end up in helium-4, one helium nucleus forms and 12 protons remain. Neglecting nucleon mass differences and binding energies, helium contains 4 of the 16 mass units. Yp ≈ 416 = 0.25 Yp is the primordial helium mass fraction in ordinary matter, not 25% of the universe’s total energy. Yp ≈ 2q1+q, q = NnNp Nn neutrons make Nn/2 helium nuclei, containing 2Nn nucleons in total. 03Stars build beyond the primordial elements Primordial nucleosynthesis produced mainly hydrogen and helium, with traces including deuterium, helium-3, and lithium. Stars turn hydrogen into more helium, then later reactions produce carbon and oxygen. Massive-star evolution can build nuclei near the iron group. Elements heavier than iron have several origins, including slow neutron capture in evolved stars and rapid neutron capture in extreme environments such as neutron-star mergers. One kind of supernova does not explain every heavy element. 04Reading light reveals the history of matter Atomic levels produce lines; line ratios and widths reveal temperature, composition, and motion. Luminosity and distance reveal energy output. Gravity and quantum physics set the conditions under which a star can exist. The equations connect different aspects of the same universe. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. Start with 2 neutrons and 14 protons and form one helium nucleus. What are helium’s number and mass fractions? Show the answer and reasoning Twelve hydrogen nuclei remain. Helium is 1/(12 + 1) ≈ 7.7% of nuclei by number, but 4/16 = 25% by mass.
